newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Teijin to set up chemical unit in Singapore.
newsitem.headline: Teijin to set up chemical unit in Singapore.

text.p: Japan's Teijin Ltd said on Monday it would set up a new company, Teijin Polycarbonate Singapore Pte Ltd, by the end of next year.

The new company, to be owned equally by Teijin and its unit Teijin Chemicals Ltd, will manufacture and sell polycarbonate resin through a new factory, due to begin operations by the end of 1998, which will have an annual production capacity of 100,000 to 150,000 tons.
It said in a statement, investment in the plant and equipment was likely to exceed 50 billion yen.
Demand for polycarbonate, a synthetic resin, has seen double digit growth in recent years and worldwide demand is expected to grow 1.7 million tons a year by 2000, it said.
Teijin Chemicals maintains a production capacity of 100,000 tons a year for polycarbonate resin in Japan, giving it the fourth largest share in the global market, it said.
The group said the new company in Singapore was being established to supply the rapidly growing Southeast Asian market and to meet the needs of its global supply system.
